summary: Installed the dnf versionlock plugin on node1 and locked curl at its current version (curl-8.12.1-4.el10). Verified the lock holds through a real dnf update (many other packages upgraded, curl untouched) and persists across a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Checked baseline: curl-8.12.1-4.el10.x86_64 on CentOS Stream 10, dnf 4.20.0
Ran dnf versionlock add curl; confirmed entry curl-0:8.12.1-4.el10.* in versionlock list
Ran a real dnf -y update which upgraded ~20 other packages (vim-minimal, tar, rsync, kernel-tools, rsyslog, qemu-guest-agent, etc.) while curl remained excluded at 8.12.1-4.el10
Captured baseline boot_id and uptime -s before restart
Issued reboot on node1; acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Verified changed boot_id and new uptime -s, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart state: curl still 8.12.1-4.el10 and versionlock entry for curl still present

evidence.requirement: curl held at current version via versionlock
evidence.summary: Baseline curl version captured; versionlock plugin installed; versionlock add curl applied and confirmed listed

evidence.requirement: Hold survives a real system update (other packages update, curl does not)
evidence.summary: dnf -y update ran to completion upgrading ~20 other packages; curl absent from the just-updated package list and check-update shows no pending curl update

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 21de1f79.../uptime 10:04:21 captured; reboot issued and acknowledged (stream closed); node reconnected; post-restart boot_id 29da1d8e.../uptime 10:08:11 differ from baseline proving restart, curl version and versionlock entry unchanged after recovery
